title: Supplier Data Transfer & Subprocessor Oversight Playbook
content:
Purpose: This working playbook is intended for Security/Legal/Procurement to operationalize contractual controls and audit practices for suppliers that: (a) receive customer data, (b) host Redwood-managed workloads in private/on‑prem deploys, or (c) operate as subprocessors (e.g., telemetry collectors, monitoring agents, model hosting partners).

Scope: Applies to any supplier that will: transfer customer data across borders, hold model weights or prompt logs, or act as a subprocessor for Redwood Inference services (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Not a replacement for the DPA template — complementary operational guidance.

Audience: Security reviewers, contract negotiators, vendor managers, solutions engineers supporting integrations.

Key objectives:
- Ensure lawful and auditable cross-border transfers with documented legal basis and technical safeguards.
- Maintain visibility and enforceability of subprocessor chains and evidence collection.
- Provide negotiation playbook and minimal-evidence checklist for SOWs/DPAs/On‑prem agreements.

Definitions (short):
- Supplier: third party providing services to Redwood.
- Subprocessor: supplier that processes regulated customer data on behalf of Redwood or its customers.
- Transfer: any movement of customer data across legal jurisdictions.

High-level controls: (1) Contractual commitments (DPA + Security Annex); (2) Technical safeguards (encryption in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM key ownership options); (3) Operational evidence (logs, audit reports, testable access reviews); (4) Audit rights & remediation timeline.

Minimal contractual language (boilerplate snippets for negotiators) — drop-in clauses to insert into supplier agreements:
- Data Transfer and Jurisdiction: "Supplier shall not transfer Customer Data outside the territories specified in Schedule X without prior written consent. Where transfers occur, Supplier will rely on an approved transfer mechanism (SCCs, BCRs) and provide evidence within 10 business days upon request."
- Subprocessor Authorization & Notification: "Supplier will list all subprocessors and obtain Redwood's advance written approval for any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data. Supplier will provide a 30-day notice for additions and a detailed data flow diagram for each."
- Key Management Option: "For Private and On‑Prem deployments, Redwood may elect customer-managed keys (BYOK). Supplier must support KMS integrations and must never hold plaintext keys for customer data under such option."
- Audit & Evidence Rights: "Supplier grants Redwood (or an accredited third‑party auditor) the right to conduct remote or onsite audits once annually and additional audits for cause with 30 days' notice. Supplier will provide SOC2 Type II, penetration test reports, and access to relevant logs for the period under review."
- Incident Notification & Preservation: "Supplier will notify Redwood of any confirmed data incident within 24 hours and preserve forensic artifacts for 90 days. Notification must include scope, root cause hypothesis, affected records, and remediation steps."

Minimal evidence checklist (fast gate for renewals/onboarding):
- Legal: Signed DPA + Security Annex; list of subprocessors; asserted transfer mechanisms (SCC/BCR) if applicable.
- Technical: Network diagram showing egress/ingress, encryption specs (TLS versions, cipher suites), KMS integration capabilities, host hardening baseline.
- Operational: Recent SOC2 Type II or equivalent (last 18 months), latest pentest summary, endpoint inventory for any agent installed in customer environments.
- Access controls: IAM roles, MFA policy, privileged access review cadence.
- Data retention & deletion: documented retention schedule and deletion proof process for customer-requested purge.

Audit types & cadence:
- Light-touch (remote evidence review): annual for low-risk suppliers or for recurring small-value services. Deliverables: SOC2, self-attestation checklist, network diagram.
- Standard (remote + log sampling): every 12 months. Deliverables: SOC2, pentest, 3 months of access logs filtered for PII access, subprocessor attestations.
- Elevated (onsite or virtual deep-dive): triggered by incident, major dataflow changes, handling of model weights or customer prompt data in plaintext, or third-party risk flagged by risk scoring. Deliverables: onsite interviews, configuration snapshots, egress rule reviews, forensic artifacts.

Evidence collection playbook (operational steps):
1) Kickoff: Risk owner opens vendor intake in JIRA (linked_artifacts above). Assign reviewer and negotiate the DPA + annex.
2) Template swap: Insert the clauses above and mark out any unsupported items. Use the redline tag: "MUST_PROVIDE" for BYOK, audit rights, and 24h incident notice.
3) Remediation items: capture as action items with due dates on contract.
4) Evidence intake: supplier uploads artifacts to a secure, time-limited S3 share or Confluence evidence page.
5) Review & final signoff: Security approves if minimal checklist satisfied; otherwise escalate to Legal for further negotiation.

On‑prem and private deployment special considerations:
- Network egress: require allowlist of outbound endpoints and deny-by-default network policies; require supplier provide explicit egress IPs and circuits.
- Physical access & evidence: for on-prem engagements, require photos of rack segregation and clear labeling of devices running Redwood workloads; require supplier-run penetration test covering physical/VM escapes where applicable.
- Model weights & ML artifacts: if supplier will host or transfer model weights, require a model manifest and a manifest verification process; require explicit licensing & usage restrictions and a mechanism to remotely wipe stored weights on contract termination.

Negotiation playbook & redlines to expect from suppliers (and suggested responses):
- Supplier: "We cannot support customer-managed keys."
  Redwood response: Offer conditional support: keep service-level keys for hosted tiers but require BYOK for Private/On‑Prem; if supplier resists, require compensating controls (HSM attestation, strict separation, shorter retention).
- Supplier: "30-day audit notice is unacceptable."
  Redwood response: Offer 30-day notice for non-critical audits, 5 business day notice for cause-based audits tied to clear escalation criteria. Keep right-to-audit language for incidents.
- Supplier: "We do not disclose subprocessors."
  Redwood response: Require categories and a minimum list (infra, monitoring, billing) and a commitment to notify on additions; allow redaction of endpoints for security but not the subprocessor identity/contractor name.

Escalation matrix (who to loop in):
- First pass: Vendor Manager + Security Reviewer (Marta Alvarez).
- If material deviation: Legal Contracts (Jacob Chen) and Product Security Lead (Ethan Cole).
- If regulatory or customer-impacting refusal: Head of Security (Priya Natarajan) + CRO for commercial exceptions.

Metrics to track for vendors under this playbook:
- Time to evidence: days from request to receipt.
- Audit completion rate: percent of suppliers completing required audits on schedule.
- Number of elevated audits triggered per quarter.
- Number of supplier exceptions granted and reason codes.

Open questions / items to refine (notes to self):
- Should we formalize a tiered fee schedule for elevated audits to offset supplier costs? (Finance input needed)
- Standardize redaction guidance for supplier-sent logs to preserve privacy while enabling review.
- Template language for model manifest: coordinate with Applied ML for fields and checksum format.

Quick checklist for solutions engineers when engaging a partner for a Private deployment:
- Confirm BYOK vs supplier KMS support before SOW.
- Ask for egress IPs and plugin list that will be installed on customer networks.
- Request preservation window for logs (min 90 days) and confirm log access method.
- Add SLA clause for wipe-on-termination and proof-of-deletion deliverable within 30 days.

Appendix A: Sample evidence request email (short):
"Hi — per our agreement we need the following evidence to complete onboarding: SOC2 Type II report, last pentest summary, list of subprocessors, network diagram showing egress IPs, and confirmation of KMS support or BYOK option. Please upload to the secure share by [date]. If you cannot provide any item, note the compensating controls and propose a timeline for remediation."
